guide.title: How the pipeline works
guide.subtitle: What staff need to take an event from booked dates to published, and what each team does along the way.

path.title: The path of a request
path.intro: Every event goes through the same five steps. The triangles on each request in the lists show where it is: green ones are done, the outlined one is the step it is on now.

draft.body: Book the dates, then fill in the event details, the Design brief and the Logistics brief. The dates are held for you for 24 hours.
draft.next: Submit sends it to Design and Logistics at the same time.

in_review.who: Design and Logistics, side by side
in_review.body: Design makes the poster. Logistics confirms the dates, times and venue as they were actually booked. Your details are frozen from here on.
in_review.next: When Design is done, the request also goes to Media.

media.who: Media, and Logistics if it is not done yet
media.body: Media prepares the announcement, using Design's poster.
media.next: When Design, Logistics and Media are all done, the request is ready.

ready.body: Every team is done. Check the date, time, place and poster one last time.

published.body: The event is created in Events with exactly what the teams confirmed, and is live: members see it and can register. From here it is run from its page in Events: responses, attendance, closing it and awarding points.

returned.title: Returned
returned.body: Design can send a request back once, with notes, within two days of receiving it. Your department then has 12 hours to fix it and press Resubmit to Design. Each day late costs a point.

cancelled.title: Cancelled
cancelled.body: The department can cancel a request at any step before it is published. Its dates go back to the calendar and every team it reached is told. A cancelled request can then be deleted for good.

rules.title: The rules in numbers
rules.intro: The system enforces these, so a button that refuses usually means one of them.

lead.text: Lead time. Today and the next three days can't be booked; the first day you can book is four days away.

length.text: The longest one request can book, as days in a row.

hold.text: How long booked dates are held while the request is a draft. Submit before the hold runs out, or the dates are released (what you filled in is kept).

oneHold.text: A department holds dates for one draft at a time. Submit or cancel it before booking the next one.

returnWindow.text: Design can return a request once, within two days of receiving it.

fix.text: To fix a returned request and resubmit it.

penalty.text: Taken off the department for every started day a fix is late, when the event is published.

hours.text: Official working hours. The details form tells you whether your event falls inside them.

page.title: Finding your way
page.intro: Everything starts on the Pipeline page.

department.title: My department
department.body: Your department's requests. What waits on you comes first (drafts to finish, returned requests, lost dates, events to publish), then what is with the teams, then what is over.

desk.title: Team desks
desk.body: For Design, Logistics and Media: what waits on your team, what Design sent back, and what your team finished. The number on the tab is what waits on you. When you finish a request, the page offers the next one, oldest first.

club.title: Whole club
club.body: Super admins only: every department's requests, grouped by who has them.

calendar.title: Booking calendar
calendar.body: Which days are free. Tap a taken day to open the request on it.

book.title: Book dates
book.body: Starts a new request. It is also in the side bar, and in the middle of the bottom bar on a phone.

bell.title: The bell
bell.body: Notifications for your department and teams: a request reached your team, Design returned yours, a team finished, it is ready to publish, Logistics changed something. Each one opens its request.

roles.title: Who does what
roles.intro: Your part is open. The others are here so you know what to expect from them.

department.name: Departments
department.who: Leaders and VPs of any department

0.title: Book dates
0.body: Press Book dates, tap the first day and then the last, and pick the department if you lead more than one. The days are now held for 24 hours.

1.title: Fill in the request
1.body: A request is five stations along the top: Event, Design, Logistics, Media and Publish. You fill in the first three: the event itself, Design's brief and Logistics' brief, and Next walks you through them. Everything saves as you type, so you can leave and come back. Each station counts what it is still missing.

2.title: Submit
2.body: Submit sends it to Design and Logistics together. The dates stay yours without a timer now, and the details can no longer be edited.

3.title: If Design returns it
3.body: Read the notes, fix the forms, and press Resubmit to Design within 12 hours. Late costs a point a day.

4.title: Publish
4.body: When it says Ready to publish, check everything and press Publish. The event goes live in Events, and you run it from there.

department.cancel: Changed your plans? Cancel request at the top of the request, at any step before publishing. Its dates go back to the calendar.

0.title: It reaches your desk
0.body: The moment a department submits, the request is on the Design desk and you are notified.

1.title: Return it if it needs fixing
1.body: Once, within two days of receiving it: Return with notes, saying exactly what to fix. The department gets 12 hours, and it comes back to you.

2.title: Upload the poster
2.body: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 10 MB. It becomes the event's image. You can replace it until the event is published.

3.title: Finish Design
3.body: Finish Design needs the poster. The request then also goes to Media.

0.title: It reaches your desk
0.body: At the same moment as Design; the two teams work at once.

1.title: Confirm the event
1.body: The confirmation opens filled in from the request: dates, each day's mode, times, venue and room, event type and description. Change whatever the booking turned out differently, then press Confirm. The event is published with exactly this.

2.title: Say why anything changed
2.body: If what you confirm differs from what was asked, give the reason; the department sees it. New dates follow the same booking rules, and the department is told.

3.title: Online days
3.body: Paste the Google Meet link, or press Generate a link to make one on the club's calendar.

4.title: Close days
4.body: Close or reopen days: pick the days, give the reason, and close them as one block. A request holding a closed day loses its dates, and its department is told.

0.title: It reaches your desk
0.body: Once Design is done, so the poster is ready.

1.title: Announce the event
1.body: Prepare the announcement from the request and its poster.

2.title: Mark Media done
2.body: When all three teams are done, the department can publish.

superAdmin.name: Super admins
superAdmin.who: Can act for every department and team

0.title: Step in only when needed
0.body: You can do any department's or team's step, and the screen says when you are acting on someone's behalf. They were already notified of their own work.

1.title: Closed and taken days
1.body: You can book a day Logistics closed, or over another request (never a published event). For each request you bump, you choose: back to a draft without dates, or cancelled. Its department is told.

2.title: The rest binds you too
2.body: The four-day lead time, four days per request, one hold per department, details frozen after submit, Design's one return, and publishing only once every team is done.

calendar.title: The calendar's colours
calendar.intro: Each day on the booking calendar is one of these.

days.locked: In the next four days. Nobody can book it.
days.banned: Logistics closed it. The reason is listed under the calendar.
days.held: A draft holds it for 24 hours. It frees up if the draft isn't submitted.
days.published: A published event is on it.

lost.a: The hold ran out, Logistics closed one of the days, or a super admin needed them. Everything you filled in is kept: open the request and press Pick new dates.

day.a: It is in the next four days, Logistics closed it, or another request has it. Your range can't cross any of those.

hold.q: It says my department already holds dates
hold.a: Only one draft holds dates at a time. Submit that draft, or cancel it, first.

submit.a: The stations along the top count what is still missing, and each station lists its own. If it says a team is not set up, tell a super admin.

change.a: The details are frozen once submitted. Logistics confirms the final dates, times and venue, so tell them; if it is bigger than that, cancel the request and start again.

changed.a: They have to say why. The reason is in the notification and on the request's Logistics station, under Confirmed by Logistics.
